title: Counit of relative Hopf modules: injectivity criterion and surjectivity under a retraction
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $H$ a commutative Hopf $k$-algebra, and $A\subseteq H$ a unital right coideal subalgebra, meaning $\Delta(A)\subseteq A\otimes_kH$. Use the Hopf identities, quotient coalgebra $C=H/HA^+$, quotient map $\pi$, and notion of relative Hopf module of [lem-sfb-relative-hopf-module-kernels]. Let $X$ be a relative Hopf module and write $R(X)=\{x:\alpha_X(x)=\pi(1)\otimes x\}$, with inclusion $j_X:R(X)\hookrightarrow X$, and let $\mu_X:H\otimes_AR(X)\to X$, $h\otimes x\mapsto hx$, be the multiplication map. (1) $\mu_X$ is injective if and only if $1_H\otimes_Aj_X:H\otimes_AR(X)\to H\otimes_AX$ is injective; this equivalence assumes neither flatness of $H$ over $A$ nor a retraction $H\to A$. (2) If there is an $A$-linear map $E:H\to A$ with $E|_A=1_A$, then $\mu_X$ is surjective: every $x\in X$ is a finite sum $\sum h_tx_t$ with $h_t\in H$ and $x_t\in R(X)$.

source.place: Bichon, arXiv:2301.05480v2, Proposition 2.7, equivalence (a) iff (b), and its implication to (c) in the case of a conditional expectation (Lemma 2.6 situation), specialized to commutative algebras. The printed proof of (a) implies (c) asserts exactness of the tensored row H tensor_A R(X) -> H tensor_A X -> H tensor_A (C tensor X) without argument; surjectivity is stated here only under the retraction E, where the A-linear map (E tensor_A 1)kappa_X^{-1} splits that row. Read at https://arxiv.org/html/2301.05480v2; local PDF WANTED in report.md.

proof.text:
Put $i=1_H\otimes_Aj_X$ and $T=\kappa_X^{-1}\alpha_X$. The coaction counit identity $(\epsilon_C\otimes1)\alpha_X=1_X$ in [lem-sfb-relative-hopf-module-kernels] makes $\alpha_X$, hence $T$, injective. The map $\mu_X$ is well-defined by tensor balancing: $(ha)x=h(ax)$ for $a\in A$. For $r\in R(X)$, compatibility of the action and coaction gives
$$\alpha_X(\mu_X(h\otimes r))=\alpha_X(hr)=\sum\pi(h_{(1)})\otimes h_{(2)}r=\kappa_X(i(h\otimes r)).$$
The tensor generators and universal property of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] extend this equality to $\alpha_X\mu_X=\kappa_Xi$. Thus $T\mu_X=i$.

source.place: Bichon, arXiv:2301.05480v2, Proposition 2.7; displayed diagram expanded using Proposition 2.2 and Lemma 2.6. Online HTML https://arxiv.org/html/2301.05480v2, sections 2.2 and 2.4; local PDF unavailable.

proof.text: Since $T$ is injective and $i=T\mu_X$, injectivity of $\mu_X$ implies injectivity of $i$. Conversely, $\mu_X(w)=\mu_X(w')$ implies $i(w)=i(w')$, so injectivity of $i$ implies $w=w'$. This proves (1), without using $E$ or flatness.

proof.text:
For (2), assume the stated retraction $E$. Let $Y=C\otimes_kX$ with the diagonal $H$-action of [lem-sfb-coideal-canonical-tensor-isomorphism], put $
u(x)=\pi(1)\otimes x$, and put $\delta=\alpha_X-
u:X	o Y$. The coaction $\alpha_X$ is $H$-linear by compatibility in [lem-sfb-relative-hopf-module-kernels]. The map $
u$ is $A$-linear: for $a\in A$, write $\Delta(a)=\sum a_{(1)}\otimes a_{(2)}$ with $a_{(1)}\in A$; since $a_{(1)}-\epsilon(a_{(1)})1\in A^+$, one has $\pi(a_{(1)})=\epsilon(a_{(1)})\pi(1)$, so $a
u(x)=\pi(1)\otimes ax$. Thus $\delta$ is $A$-linear and may be tensored over $A$.

source.place: Bichon, arXiv:2301.05480v2, Proposition 2.7; displayed diagram expanded using Proposition 2.2 and Lemma 2.6. Online HTML https://arxiv.org/html/2301.05480v2, sections 2.2 and 2.4; local PDF unavailable.

proof.text:
Write $D=1_H\otimes_A\delta$. Naturality of $\kappa$ for the $H$-linear map $\alpha_X:X\to Y$ gives
$$\kappa_Y(1_H\otimes_A\alpha_X)=(1_C\otimes_k\alpha_X)\kappa_X.$$
For the other term, direct evaluation on a tensor generator gives
$$\kappa_Y(1_H\otimes_A\nu)(h\otimes x)=\sum\pi(h_{(1)})\otimes\pi(h_{(2)})\otimes h_{(3)}x=(\Delta_C\otimes1_X)\kappa_X(h\otimes x).$$
Here the middle expression uses the diagonal action on $Y$, and coassociativity of $H$ gives the three factors in that order; no cocommutativity is used. Consequently
$$\kappa_YDT=\big((1_C\otimes\alpha_X)-(\Delta_C\otimes1_X)\big)\alpha_X=0$$
by coassociativity of $\alpha_X$. Injectivity of $\kappa_Y$ gives $DT=0$. The cited canonical-isomorphism node applies to $Y$ as an $H$-module, without a flatness assumption.

source.place: Bichon, arXiv:2301.05480v2, Proposition 2.7; displayed diagram expanded using Proposition 2.2 and Lemma 2.6. Online HTML https://arxiv.org/html/2301.05480v2, sections 2.2 and 2.4; local PDF unavailable.

proof.text:
Define $e:H\otimes_AX\to X$ by $e(h\otimes x)=E(h)x$ and $q=e\kappa_X^{-1}:Y\to X$. Balancing follows from $E(ha)=E(h)a$; commutativity also gives $E(ah)=aE(h)$, so $e$, and hence $q$, is $A$-linear. By [lem-sfb-coideal-coinvariant-projection], $q\alpha_X=j_Xp_X$, where $p_X:X\to R(X)$ is $A$-linear. Also $\kappa_X(1\otimes x)=\pi(1)\otimes x=\nu(x)$ and $E(1)=1$, so $q\nu=1_X$. Therefore
$$q\delta=j_Xp_X-1_X.$$
For $z=T(x)$, step 4 gives $Dz=0$. Applying $1_H\otimes_Aq$ and using tensor compatibility with differences and composition yields
$$0=(1_H\otimes_Aq)Dz=(1_H\otimes_A(j_Xp_X))z-z.$$
Thus $w=(1_H\otimes_Ap_X)z\in H\otimes_AR(X)$ satisfies $iw=z$. This proves the needed lifting assertion directly; tensoring an arbitrary kernel sequence has not been assumed to preserve exactness.

source.place: Bichon, arXiv:2301.05480v2, Proposition 2.7; displayed diagram expanded using Proposition 2.2 and Lemma 2.6. Online HTML https://arxiv.org/html/2301.05480v2, sections 2.2 and 2.4; local PDF unavailable.

proof.text: Step 1 and step 5 give $\alpha_X\mu_X(w)=\kappa_Xi(w)=\kappa_Xz=\alpha_X(x)$. Apply $\epsilon_C\otimes1_X$ to conclude $\mu_X(w)=x$. Every tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]; absorb any $A$-coefficients into their $H$-factors. Writing $w=\sum_t h_t\otimes x_t$ with $x_t\in R(X)$ therefore gives $x=\sum_t h_tx_t$. This proves (2).
